pilot_notice: PILOT. These figures come from one coder's first pass on a stratified random sample of 300 keyword-matched 2023 Media Cloud stories from Associated Press, CNN, Fox News, The New York Times and The Washington Post (AP 31, a census of its frame; CNN 29; Fox 95; NYT 80; WaPo 65). Six sample rows could not be coded (fetch failures). No second coder or agreement rate yet. There are fewer than 20 included incidents, so a point-estimate index is not published. A zero Black-on-White cell is shown as 0 of N plus the exact one-sided 95% lower bound. The keyword frame is not a random sample of interracial incidents.

disclosure_track.reason: The 2023 keyword sample cannot support the disclosure track: inclusion required race to be stated, so disclosure is 100% by construction, and there are no knowable Black-on-White incidents in the file.

USA.frame_caveat: The keyword frame is a likely cause of the zero Black-on-White cell. Under a random frame, P(0 of 12 | NCVS share 0.766) is about 2.7e-8, but only 91 of 1,648 frame phrase-hits were B-direction, and none of the sampled B-phrase rows was a crime incident.

data_gaps.reason: The public point-estimate index, and every outlet point-estimate index cell, stay pending until an incident-based sample (starting from official or news-of-record incidents, then finding all coverage, including stories that omit race) can support them. A zero cell is still shown as 0 of N plus the exact one-sided 95% lower bound.
no crime baseline: no NCVS or other official U.S. table records ethnic Jewish offenders against non-Hispanic White victims; story counts only, no index.

Homicide stories are compared with FBI SHR Expanded Homicide Data Table 6 (single victim/single offender, 2023: White-on-Black 324, Black-on-White 726). NCVS covers nonfatal violent incidents and excludes homicide. The two are not pooled into one point-estimate index. The preferred country lower bound uses the NCVS ratio on the mixed keyword sample and is labelled as such.
A per-capita rate view is required next to the raw SHR counts. No cited population denominator for Table 6's race categories (race, not Hispanic origin) has been joined, so the rates are pending.

the story frame was built from keyword queries, most of them anti-Black framings ("white supremacist", "anti-Black", "racially motivated", "hate crime"); only "anti-white" and "Black supremacist" target the reverse framing. Black-on-White crime stories that use none of these phrases are not in the frame, so the pilot frame is expected to under-sample them. This is a pre-registered alternative explanation (label convention, query misfire).
single coder (joseph-a) so far; the method requires a second coder and an agreement rate before results are reported as findings.
BJS published only percentages (Table 14) for 2018, not counts; count is null and not derived.

judgement_calls: The Coverage Distortion Index (CDI) is the methods name for the calculation behind the Antiwhite media bias index. It is not a second public index. cdi is null whenever a cell is 0, when both cells are 0, or when a point estimate would otherwise be unpublished.

No +0.5, or any other constant, is added to manufacture a point-estimate index. Earlier +0.5 figures (including Fox 29.4× and CNN 16.3×, and the pooled pilot CDIs) are artifacts and must not be published as findings.

When a direction is 0, the published figure is 0 of N plus the Clopper-Pearson exact one-sided 95% lower bound. The preferred country inference is the incident-level bound (stories of the same incident are a cluster). Story-level bounds are stored for transparency and for outlet rows.

Insufficient data means fewer than 20 included incidents overall (unweighted, all directions, including other). A zero cell is not Insufficient data by itself; the US 2023 pilot is Insufficient data because it has 6 (strict) or 8 (broad) included incidents.
Outlet point-estimate index cells are pending until an incident-based sample is complete. A zero at an outlet is still 0 of N plus the bound.

Rates (headline_rate, pct_first_para, photo_rate) and stance counts use included stories (include=true, any direction, including 'other'); each rate's denominator is given in the matching *_n field. pct_first_para = share whose first racial mention is in the headline (para 1) or first body paragraph (para 2).
stories_total = all rows for the outlet in the stories file, i.e. keyword-matched Media Cloud hits (volume only), not coded crime stories.
Sample weights are not applied to the published counts: they are constant within an outlet, so the within-outlet ratio is the same weighted or unweighted. Thresholds use unweighted counts.
include=dup is not counted as included.

The Strict / Broad toggle follows the 19 Nov rules: Broad counts a "white supremacist" or "white nationalist" label, or "espoused White supremacist beliefs", as White; liking or sharing such content does not. ethnic Jewish or Palestinian (and similar) labels are coded direction=other.
Homicide and non-fatal comparisons are stored separately and are not pooled into one published point-estimate index.
